exposure: meconium staining of amniotic fluid (thin vs. thick)
outcome: mode of delivery (vaginal vs. caesarean section)
cohort: 200 women in labor with singleton cephalic pregnancies complicated by meconium-stained amniotic fluid.
finding: Thick meconium-stained amniotic fluid was associated with a higher incidence of abnormal CTG, lower 5-minute Apgar scores, Meconium Aspiration Syndrome, and neonatal mortality compared to thin meconium.
mod_finding: Caesarean section rates were higher in the thick meconium group (77.1%) compared to the thin meconium group (64.3%).
